capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs (2022) gives 88 kWh usable (2021) for the Extended Range; the page does not name the GT. The GT shares the ER pack (376 cells, 2023 Ford sheet), so 88 kWh.

capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs (2022) gives 98.8 kWh total for the Extended Range pack; the GT shares that pack (376 cells, 2023 Ford sheet).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia lists NMC packs (LG Energy Solution) for the launch-era Standard and Extended Range.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: Mach-E LFP pack reads 347.8 V nominal (Electrek); the NMC packs share the same architecture, so 400 V class. Class inferred from the figure.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Ford Canada says its electric vehicles use navigation-triggered battery preconditioning (route planning or choosing a DC fast charger in Connected Navigation, Google Maps or Apple Maps EV Routing). The cited page is silent on any manual control and on model years; I found no manual battery-preconditioning control documented in Ford support pages or owner forums (owners have asked for one since 2021), so automatic_with_navigation is the best fit, not a proven fact. Cars from 2021 and 2022 may predate the navigation trigger (the Ford Canada navigation page says earlier model years received it by software update), so the value for this model year is unconfirmed.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: the 2022 Ford spec sheet lists up to 150 kW for this pack and Wikipedia lists the same 115 / 150 kW for 2020-22, but the basis is unproven: InsideEVs (2022) says Ford "improved the fast charging curve" for 2022, so the 2021 peak may differ.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia infobox lists 11 kW onboard AC for the Mach-E (Ford owners cite 10.5 kW output / 11.3-11.5 kW at 48 A); no onboard-charger change found 2021-2026. Wikipedia does not name a market, so the Canadian car is unproven.
